issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes only the endpoint condition V(x_{k+1}) <= epsilon from V(x_k) <= epsilon. It does not establish the stronger stated inclusion of the whole Euler segment in U^epsilon, which is part of the theorem and of the later minimization over gains satisfying that inclusion.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing short argument that the quadratic upper bound along the segment is convex and has both endpoints at most epsilon, or weaken the statement to endpoint positive invariance and adjust the minimization premise.

issues.title: Tube inclusion in optimal-gain theorem not proved

(\tau-1) \Gamma h F{\tilde{\varepsilon}} \leq \frac{c-1}{2} H_{\min}\quad\text{and} \quad \frac{(\tau-1)\Gamma}{c H_{\min}} M_{\tilde{\varepsilon}} \leq \frac{c-1}{2} H_{\min}.
Since $(\tau-1)h \leq nh \leq T_{\mathrm{update}} + h$, the former inequality reduces to $(T_{\mathrm{update}} + h) \Gamma F_{\tilde{\varepsilon}} \leq \frac{c-1}{2} H_{\min}$.

there exists $T_{\mathrm{update}}>0$ and $h_0 > 0$ such that for all $h \in (0, h_0)$, $x_k$ generated from Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive_gain_euler_period} satisfies $V(x_k) \leq \varepsilon$ for all $k$.

issues.failure_explanation: The first possible violation at the end of an update block (ell = n) is not considered. More substantively, for n = ceil(T_update/h), the accumulated Hessian-drift bound contains (tau-1) M_tilde/(c H_min), which is bounded by (T_update/h + 1) M_tilde/(c H_min). For fixed T_update > 0 and M_tilde > 0 this term is unbounded as h -> 0, so the sufficient inclusion conditions cannot be made to hold uniformly for all h in (0,h0). The proof's smallness argument at h proportional to h0(tilde) does not extend to smaller h.

failure_location.quote: let $\tau$ be the smallest $\ell \in \{1, 2, \dots n-1\}$ such that $V(x_{k_0 + \ell}) > \tilde{\varepsilon}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Repair the proof by including the final step, using tau (or n) terms in the Hessian-drift estimate, and choosing the intermediate sublevel (possibly as a small power of h) so that the cumulative (T_update/h) M_tilde term is uniformly small; then apply the local invariance argument to each update block.
issues.overall_effect: The guaranteed preservation of V <= epsilon for the time-domain update-period algorithm is unreliable as written, and the advertised consequence that the computational cost approaches the fixed-gain cost as h -> 0 is unsupported.
issues.title: Time-based gain-update period proof fails as h tends to zero
issues.why_classification: The fix requires a nonroutine reoptimization of the block estimates and a missing case, but the stated fixed-time update-period guarantee can in principle be preserved without excluding small h or changing the main theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose says both the adaptive and fixed optimal-gain feedback integrators deliver the highest accuracy across the tested Kepler step sizes, but the same section states that the fixed optimal-gain method diverges at the largest tested step h=0.1. A diverging method cannot outperform the benchmark across the entire tested range.
